description: Pin-replay determinism (CPD-5, CPD5-23): the release layer (RELEASE_DEFAULTS) then `layers` resolve to an EffectiveRunConfig whose digest is `configDigest`; with `pin`'s members and schemaVersion 1 the ResolvedRunConfig's digest is `digest` (canonical JSON of every member but digest). Node's PolicyRunConfigPinner and Python's pinning module give these answers; member order never changes them. A case with `parent` is a child's pin: the release, then the parent's `effectiveConfig` as a `parent` layer (each dimension the table exposes to `parent`, at its own path), then `layers`; the parent's entries of the dimensions no `parent` layer may set are copied to the result as they are, in place of the release's where the release names the row (`expected.inherited` names each entry the child's own resolution did not give), `configDigest` is the digest of that config, and the pin's `llm` is the parent's, unless the case's `pin` names an `llm` of its own: a child whose role set its model (MA1) is pinned to that model's configured entry.

cases.description: agent narrows the org's budgets; the request narrows turns
a request that widens the agent's cost ceiling is refused, naming it
MA1: a model per role, chosen inside the org's routes
a child: the parent's values as a parent layer, the request narrowing them
an engine agent: its profile narrows the release's, the org's approvals apply
a user layer may not set a ceiling

a child's pin (release, its parent's pin as a parent layer, its request): the parent's resolved approvals with two flow rules are read as they were resolved and narrowed by the request; the dimensions no parent layer may set (the rollout stages) are the parent's entries as they are; llm is the parent's

a child's pin names the owner of the agent as its parent's pin holds it, whatever its own subject says (a spawn has no definition in hand): scope is computed from `subject` and the parent's scope, and what the owner shared with the agent stays visible in the child

MA1: an agent whose definition sets a model per sub-agent role (`models.roles`, inside the routes it grants) under the org's cost ceilings per role (`models.roleCostCeilings`); the second org layer is the configured-models ceiling

MA1: a role-assigned child of PV-9 (role `researcher`): its request names the role's route as `models.primary`, inside its parent's routes; the roles and the cost ceilings are its parent's; its `llm` is the role's configured entry, not its parent's

CPD-10 R3: an org the capability migration recorded as migrated carries rollout.CONTROL_PLANE_CAPABILITIES in its layer (the release holds no such row), so the pin's config holds it true and its effective set is the authority for the run's items

CPD-10 R3: a child's pin takes its parent's rollout.CONTROL_PLANE_CAPABILITIES verbatim (no layer below the org carries rollout rows), so a migrated org's child run reads its own effective set as the authority too
SIGNIN-5: a run admitted on the person's own Claude plan narrows accountKinds to user_plan_sandbox_login, which the release default lists, so CONTROL_PLANE_PIN=on pins it
SIGNIN-5: the release default still lists no injected plan kind: a run narrowed to user_plan_injected is refused, naming the dimension
SIGNIN-5: an org whose engine profile ceiling leaves the plan kind out still removes it: a run narrowed to user_plan_sandbox_login is refused at the request
